claims.text: The initial material is an equiatomic FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
The FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase FCC crystal at 300 K.
The initial crystal contains a low density of vacancy clusters and solute inhomogeneities.
Yield strength is relatively insensitive to strain rate from 10^8 to 10^10 s^-1.
Yield strength decreases with increasing temperature.
Deformation is mediated by Shockley partial dislocations and intrinsic stacking faults.
Strain-rate-insensitive yielding arises because nucleation is governed by local chemical barriers at solute clusters rather than by dislocation motion or annihilation kinetics.
Shockley partials nucleate preferentially at vacancy clusters or solute-rich regions where local lattice distortion lowers the critical emission stress.
Dislocation nucleation is athermal and controlled by a local reduction of the Peierls barrier at vacancy clusters.
The <11-1> loading direction has a higher maximum yield strength than <110>.
The <11-1> direction has a higher resolved shear stress factor on the primary {111}<112> slip system than <110>.
A higher orientation-specific critical stacking-fault-energy barrier contributes to the greater yield strength under <11-1> loading.
The geometric projection under <11-1> loading delays nucleation until a higher macroscopic stress is reached.
The yield stress under <11-1> loading will be approximately 15–20% higher than under <110> loading.
The yield stress drop will coincide with Shockley partial emission from vacancy clusters.
The HCP-like regions are transient intrinsic stacking faults rather than a bulk HCP phase transformation.
Cr-rich local environments have high stacking-fault energy that stabilizes the transient intrinsic stacking faults.
HCP-coordinated atoms will remain strictly confined to stacking-fault ribbons without a continuously growing HCP region.
An HCP-coordinated region extending more than 2 nm beyond a single-fault width would indicate a true phase transformation.
CNA/BAD spatial mapping and a local stacking-fault-energy profile can discriminate a planar intrinsic stacking fault from a stable HCP phase.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis invokes 'athermal thermal activation,' the mechanism calls nucleation athermal, and the boundary states that thermal activation is significant. These descriptions of the rate-controlling process are mutually inconsistent.

The proposal says <11-1> loading has a higher resolved-shear-stress factor but also says this delays nucleation and raises the applied yield stress. For a fixed critical resolved shear stress, a higher Schmid factor would ordinarily produce yielding at a lower applied stress; the additional orientation-specific barrier is asserted but not coherently quantified.
The initial state affirmatively specifies pre-existing vacancy clusters, while the uncertainty field says these sites may instead be dynamic solute clusters rather than static vacancies.
